question: How does AFFiNE store a document's content in edgeless (whiteboard) mode: how does it relate to the same document in page mode, where do shapes and drawings live, and how are position, stacking order and grouping represented?

points.text: an edgeless document is the same document as in page mode, made of the same blocks: switching modes converts nothing, and the same doc can be attached to a page editor or an edgeless editor
a surface block, by default the root block's first child, is the container for the whiteboard's graphical content

shapes, brush strokes, connectors and other drawings are not blocks but surface elements (such as `ShapeElement`, `BrushElement` and `ConnectorElement`), kept in the surface block's `elements` field and drawn on an HTML5 canvas

flowing content (paragraphs, lists, images and so on) sits in note blocks: page mode shows the notes in their order among the root block's children, while in edgeless mode a document can be split into several notes placed separately on the canvas

a block can sit in one of two places: as a direct child of the surface block (edgeless-only, placed anywhere on the canvas, without nesting) or outside it as in page mode (shared with page mode, nestable, laid out inside its note); some types, such as images, can be in either
every note block, every child of the surface block and every surface element has an `xywh` field giving its absolute position and size on the canvas
stacking order on the canvas comes from an `index` field compared across those blocks and the surface elements, with fractional indexing (as in Figma), not from the order of the block tree

content is associated in two ways: frame blocks, surface-only blocks that mark an area, where moving a frame moves whatever lies inside it by geometry rather than by nesting (and presentation mode steps through frames); and group elements, surface elements that store their children's IDs, take their size from them and can nest

answer:
Edgeless mode doesn't store a separate copy of the document. It adds data to the same Yjs doc that page mode uses. I read this from the code but did not run AFFiNE to check it.

**Relation to page mode**
- The page-mode block tree is `affine:page` → `affine:note` blocks → paragraphs, lists and so on. Edgeless mode reuses it.
- Each `affine:note` block (`blocksuite/affine/model/src/blocks/note/note-model.ts`) also carries edgeless props: `xywh`, `index` (default `'a0'`) and an `edgeless` style object. This is how a note appears as a card on the canvas.
- A note's `displayMode` controls where it shows. It can be edgeless-only, or visible in both the doc and edgeless views.
- The `affine:surface` block is the page's second child. It is the edgeless layer, and its schema declares `parent: ['@root']`. Page mode ignores it.

**Where shapes and drawings live**
- Shapes, brush strokes, highlighter strokes, connectors, groups, mindmaps and canvas text are not blocks. They live inside the surface block's single `elements` prop. That prop is a boxed `Y.Map<Y.Map>`, keyed by element id (`SurfaceBlockSchema` in `blocksuite/affine/blocks/surface/src/surface-model.ts`). Each value is a Y.Map of that element's props, with a `type` field such as `shape`, `brush`, `connector` or `group`.
- The model classes are in `blocksuite/affine/model/src/elements/*`.
- Rich objects are real child blocks of the surface: `affine:frame`, `affine:image`, `affine:bookmark`, `affine:attachment`, `affine:embed-*` and `affine:edgeless-text`.
- Notes, frames and images are therefore blocks, while shapes and strokes are entries in `elements`.

**Position, stacking and grouping**
- **Position:** every element and every edgeless block has `xywh`. It is a serialized string such as `"[x,y,w,h]"`. Elements also have `rotate`.
- **Stacking:** each element and block has a fractional-indexing string in `index`, generated with `generateKeyBetween`. Insertion order is encoded in the string, so inserting between two items needs only one new key. This also merges cleanly across collaborators. `blocksuite/framework/std/src/gfx/layer.ts` sorts by this string to produce the z-order.
- **Grouping:** a `group` element (`blocksuite/affine/model/src/elements/group/group.ts`) has a `children` prop that is a `Y.Map<boolean>` of child id → `true`, plus a `title` Y.Text. A child can be an element or a block, and the group's bounds come from them. The group is the parent and the children don't point back to it. Child ids are exposed as `childIds`. Connectors refer to their endpoints by id.
